Question_text: FlyAway is an airline business. It is in the tertiary sector. It offers low-price flights for business customers in country J. Customers have to pay extra for luggage and food on the flight. It is a very competitive market. The Marketing manager knows that improving customer service is important. Bookings and advertising are done through FlyAway's ticket shops and its website. The Marketing manager cannot decide whether to close its ticket shops and use only e-commerce.
image: Table 1: Selected information about two of FlyAway's routes. The table has three columns: 'Route', 'Average number of passengers per flight', 'Average price per ticket ($)', and 'Break-even number of passengers per flight'. It contains data for two routes. Route 1 has 85 passengers, $80 ticket price, and 70 break-even passengers. Route 2 has 110 passengers, $60 ticket price, and 90 break-even passengers.
Sub_topic: Use of internet, social media for promotion
Use for decisions: higher price impact
Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'tertiary sector'?
Calculate the revenue gained from an average flight on route 2.
Identify and explain two ways in which break-even information could help FlyAway.
Identify and explain two ways in which FlyAway could improve customer service.
Do you think FlyAway should use only e-commerce? Justify your answer.

Question_text: CGM makes high quality shoes using job production. The production method makes use of specialisation. CGM operates in a niche market. CGM managers know that all business activity creates external costs, so they always try to act in ways that protect the environment. The Operations Director wants to increase profit. CGM could either buy cheaper raw materials or introduce new technology into the production process. The new technology would cost $30000 and could reduce the number of employees from 30 to 26.
Sub_topic: Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Different objectives: survival, growth, profit, market share
Changes from technology: computers in design, manufacturing
Situations for downsizing: automation, reduced demand

Parts.part_text: Identify two advantages of specialisation.
What is meant by 'external cost'?
Identify and explain two ways in which CGM could try to protect the environment.
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to CGM of using job production.
Do you think CGM should introduce new technology into the production process? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Yanis owns a busy restaurant in the city centre. He employs 4 skilled chefs and 6 workers to serve in the restaurant. All employees are on part-time contracts. The chefs are paid a high hourly wage rate, but receive no bonuses. Yanis is worried that too many chefs leave. He is thinking of other ways in which he could motivate the chefs. Yanis wants to open another restaurant but is worried about problems linked to growth. He has prepared a balance sheet as part of his business plan. An extract is shown in Table 2. The current ratio was 1.2:1 in 2016.
image: Table 2: Extract from balance sheet as at 30 September 2017 ($000). The table has two columns: 'Non-current assets' and 'Amount'. It lists financial figures: Non-current assets (160), Current assets (60), Current liabilities (40), Non-current liabilities (120).
Sub_topic: Contents of business plan, assistance to entrepreneurs
Reasons people work, meaning of motivation
Concept of human needs, Maslow’s hierarchy
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing
Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion
Interpret, make deductions: financing, assets, inventory sale
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio

Parts.part_text: Identify two main parts (other than finance) of a business plan.
What is meant by 'non-current assets'?
Calculate the current ratio as at 30 September 2017.
Explain what the two current ratio results show about Yanis's business.
Identify two possible problems for Yanis if he expands his business. Explain what he might do to overcome each problem.
Do you think Yanis should change the way he motivates his chefs? Justify your answer.

Question_text: VIS provides a range of insurance services including insurance for cars and electrical products. Last year retained profit decreased. The Managing Director blames higher taxation and also thinks that some markets have become more competitive. Customer complaints have also increased. The Managing Director plans to change the business organisational structure by removing both the regional directors and regional managers. She said: 'Shorter chains of command may help. I know some employees may need training.' She cannot decide on a suitable method of communication to inform employees about the changes to the organisational structure.
Sub_topic: Hierarchical structures: levels, span of control, chain of command, chain of tall/short
Importance of delegation, trust vs control
Roles: directors, managers, supervisors, employees, inter-relationships
Functions: planning, organising, coordinating, commanding, controlling
Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit
Importance of training to business, employees
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Benefits, limitations of methods, including IT
How barriers arise, problems of ineffective communication

Parts.part_text: Identify two reasons why markets can become more competitive.
Identify two methods of training that a business might use.
Identify and explain two ways in which higher taxation might affect VIS.
Identify and explain two advantages to VIS of changing its organisational structure.
Recommend the best method of communication VIS should use to inform employees about the changes to its organisational structure. Justify your answer.
